item.title: Compute brief — 4 September 2026
item.description: The binding constraint on US AI campuses this week is not another GPU list print — Lambda H100 is still $3.99 and B200 $6.69 on a clean confirm day — it is who is allowed to sell the transformers and inverters that hook those racks to the grid. Executive Order 14420 (26 Aug) puts foreign-produced bulk-power equipment under DOE emergency authority, with implementing rules due in 120 days; CNBC and Wood Mackenzie on 2–3 Sep spell out why that lands on data centers first. Crusoe’s reported $3B round at a $30B valuation (TechCrunch/Bloomberg, 3 Sep) shows neocloud balance sheets still clearing, but Howard–Solstice 59336 remains without a final CCN order. Countries: United States: EO 14420 (26 Aug) authorizes DOE to restrict foreign-produced BPS equipment (transformers, inverters, BESS, UPS, controls). Rules due ~120 days; CNBC 3 Sep frames China share in DC power stack as the exposure. China: Covered Foreign Entity pathway plus reported China share (~30% some transformer/switchgear categories; >40% US battery imports per Johns Hopkins quotes in CNBC) is the geopolitical hinge of the order. United States / Texas: PUCT 59336 Howard–Solstice still HOLD: Interchange shows Commission Counsel memorandum + protest filings 3 Sep, no final order after Order No. 1 reopened the record on 28 Aug.
